walkthroughs.body_html:
Foundations of Environmental Systems — a core area of Environmental Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Foundations of Environmental Systems brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Foundations of Environmental Systems.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

What is the difference between ozone depletion and climate change?
options: Two distinct issues - ozone depletion is about UV protection (caused mainly by CFCs); climate change is about heat trapping (caused mainly by CO2).
Ozone depletion causes climate change directly.
They are the same problem.
Predators have weaker immune systems.
Industrial chemicals being dumped.
Dissolved CO2 forms carbonic acid, lowering ocean pH.
Acid rain falling on the ocean.
Predators have weaker immune systems.

mcqs.q: Why are top predators most affected by persistent pollutants like mercury?
options: Biomagnification concentrates pollutants at each trophic level up the food chain.
Industrial chemicals being dumped.
Predators have weaker immune systems.
Predators are exposed to more pollution directly.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Earth Summit”?
options: 1992 Rio Conference produced Agenda 21, UNFCCC and CBD; landmark in environmental governance.
Analysing environment as interlinked open systems with inputs, outputs, flows, feedbacks.
Meeting present needs without compromising ability of future generations to meet theirs (Brundtland 1987).
Individual rational use of shared resource leads to collective ruin (Hardin 1968 in Science).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Precautionary principle”?
options: 1992 Rio Conference produced Agenda 21, UNFCCC and CBD; landmark in environmental governance.
Where serious damage threatens, lack of full scientific certainty should not delay preventive action.
Worldview shaping how individuals/societies evaluate environmental issues; ecocentric, anthropocentric, technocentric (IBDP categorisation).
Individual rational use of shared resource leads to collective ruin (Hardin 1968 in Science).
